team.title: Founder & Reviewer of Record
team.text: HerbAlly was created and is curated by Yasser Bheekun, MLT (OPTMQ · CSMLS) — a Medical Laboratory Technologist holding a DEC in Biomedical Laboratory Technology (Dawson College) working in a hospital laboratory at the McGill University Health Centre in Montreal, Quebec. Yasser progressively reviews and validates herb profiles against primary clinical and regulator references; each entry displays a status badge showing whether it has been human-verified, AI-summarized, or flagged for re-review. Editorial review is not physician medical care.

methodologyContent.title: Our Methodology
methodologyContent.subtitle: How we research, grade, and present herbal medicine information
methodologyContent.questionsDesc: We're committed to transparency. If you have questions about how we grade evidence or want to report an error, please reach out.

evidenceGrading.title: Evidence Grading System
evidenceGrading.content:
Every efficacy claim in HerbAlly is graded from A to Traditional Use for a specific studied indication, extract, and dose (never as a blanket safety endorsement for an entire plant):

**A (Strong Evidence)**: Multiple randomized controlled trials (RCTs), systematic reviews, or meta-analyses demonstrating consistent positive results for a defined indication and preparation. Example: Ginger for pregnancy-related nausea has Grade A efficacy evidence, which does not automatically mean every ginger dose or extract is proven safe across all stages of pregnancy.

**B (Moderate Evidence)**: Some human RCTs or well-designed observational studies showing positive results, limited by sample size, duration, or study quality. Example: Ashwagandha for stress reduction.

**C (Limited / Preliminary Clinical Evidence)**: Early human clinical trials, small pilot studies, or observational human case series requiring confirmation. Preclinical animal, in vitro (cell), and in silico (computational) findings are labeled separately by study design below.

**Traditional Use**: Long history of traditional use (100+ years) with ethnographic or historical pharmacopoeia documentation, distinct from modern controlled clinical trials.

**D (Anecdotal)**: Anecdotal reports or theoretical plausibility without clinical data. Flagged clearly with caution.

sourceHierarchy.title: Source Hierarchy
sourceHierarchy.content:
We prioritize primary regulatory and clinical sources in this order:

1. **Regulatory Monographs & Product Registers**: Health Canada NHP Monographs & Licensed Natural Health Products Database (LNHPD), European Medicines Agency (EMA / HMPC)
2. **Government Clinical References**: NIH National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH), NIH LiverTox hepatotoxicity database
3. **Systematic Reviews & Clinical Trials**: Cochrane Database, PubMed-indexed peer-reviewed RCTs and pharmacokinetic interaction studies
4. **Pharmacopoeias & Historical Materia Medica**: WHO Monographs, Commission E, US Dispensatory (1918), British/European Pharmacopoeias (marked clearly as Traditional Use)

We avoid: Marketing claims, unreviewed manufacturer testimonials, and unsourced blogs.

safetyAssessment.title: Safety Assessment
safetyAssessment.content:
Safety data is evaluated separately from efficacy:

**Contraindications**: Conditions where the herb should not be used (e.g., pregnancy, liver disease, specific medication interactions)

**Precautions**: Conditions requiring medical supervision or dose adjustment

**Drug Interactions**: Based on pharmacokinetic data and case reports. Severity classified as:
- Contraindicated: Never combine
- Severe: High risk; require monitoring
- Moderate: Moderate risk; consult healthcare provider
- Mild: Low risk; monitor for side effects

**Pregnancy & Nursing**: Assessed against the current FDA Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLR) narrative framework, EMA HMPC monograph Section 4.6, NIH LactMed, and Health Canada NHP monographs. We explicitly distinguish evidence availability (Unknown — insufficient human data) from precautionary avoidance recommendations (Not recommended).

monographProcess.title: Monograph Creation Process
monographProcess.content:
Published profiles follow a traceable five-step workflow with transparent status labelling:

1. **Source Extraction**: Official regulator monographs (Health Canada, EMA HMPC), government summaries (NCCIH, LiverTox), and PubMed citations are linked verbatim.
2. **Taxonomic Verification**: Botanical binomials and plant parts are cross-checked against GBIF, ITIS, and NCBI Taxonomy for nomenclature only (never for clinical dosing or safety).
3. **Safety & Interaction Mapping**: Drug interactions, hepatotoxicity ratings, and pregnancy/lactation cautions are mapped against clinical and regulator references, and dose calculators are suppressed on high-risk or toxic plants.
4. **Progressive Editorial Review**: Entries are progressively verified against primary references by Yasser Bheekun, MLT (OPTMQ · CSMLS) — editorial checking of source alignment and safety framing, not physician clinical care.
5. **Transparent Labelling & Corrections**: Every profile displays its review state ('Source-checked', 'Clinician-signed', 'AI-summarized', 'Not human-reviewed', or 'Needs re-review'). Only verified clinician-signed entries display a clinical sign-off date; safety corrections are prioritized.

transparency.title: Transparency & Limitations
transparency.content:
We believe in honest communication about what we know and don't know:

**What We Do**: Provide evidence-based summaries of herbal medicine research
**What We Don't Do**: Make medical recommendations, replace doctor consultation, or guarantee outcomes

**Limitations**:
- Herb quality varies by source; we cannot verify your specific product
- Individual responses to herbs vary significantly
- Traditional evidence doesn't always translate to modern clinical efficacy
- Research gaps exist for many herbs

**Our Bias**: We are committed to evidence over tradition. If traditional use conflicts with negative clinical evidence, we highlight the clinical findings.

activeCompounds.title: Active Compound Analysis
activeCompounds.content:
For each herb, we identify:

**Primary Actives**: The compounds most likely responsible for observed effects
**Mechanism**: How these compounds interact with human physiology
**Bioavailability**: How well compounds are absorbed and utilized
**Standardization**: Whether commercial extracts standardize for these compounds

This information helps users understand:
- Why different brands may vary in effectiveness
- What to look for on supplement labels
- How formulation affects bioavailability (e.g., curcumin + piperine)

overview.title: 1. Overview
overview.text: HerbAlly is free to use and most of the site works without an account. Some features, such as saving a garden, saving calculations or keeping chat history, need an account or create an anonymous session. This policy explains what is stored, where it is stored, and the choices you have.

infoWeCollect.title: 2. Information We Collect
infoWeCollect.text: Depending on how you use HerbAlly, we may collect:
infoWeCollect.chatMessages: Questions sent to the Virtual Herbalist may be processed by Ollama Cloud to generate replies. Signed-in conversations can be saved to your account; guest conversations may be saved to a session linked to the herbally-guest-id cookie.
infoWeCollect.analytics: Cloudflare Web Analytics collects cookieless, privacy-first aggregate traffic counts and Core Web Vitals performance telemetry.
infoWeCollect.cookies: HerbAlly uses cookies for language preference, guest sessions and authentication. Your browser may also store garden entries and notes and recent searches. If advertising is enabled in the future, Google and its partners may use cookies or device identifiers.
infoWeCollect.notCollect: We do not ask for your name or email unless you create an account or make a donation. We do not sell personal information.

howWeUse.title: 3. How We Use Your Information
items: Generate AI responses in the Virtual Herbalist
Save optional account data, including your garden, saved calculations and chat history
Process donations through Stripe and keep the necessary accounting record
Improve our herb database and AI responses using aggregate analytics
Remember your language preference across visits
Ensure the security and integrity of our platform

thirdParty.title: 4. Third-Party Services
thirdParty.text: HerbAlly uses the following third-party services:
thirdParty.supabase: Self-hosted PostgreSQL / Supabase stack operated in Montreal, Quebec, Canada — stores optional user accounts, saved health profiles, garden entries, dosage history, and aggregate donation logs.
thirdParty.vercel: Cloudflare — DNS, TLS edge proxy, Cloudflare Tunnel, and cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics protecting traffic to our Montreal origin server.
thirdParty.stripe: Stripe — payment processing for donations. HerbAlly never sees or stores your card details. Stripe provides us the donor name, email and payment status so the donation can be recorded.
thirdParty.ollamaCloud: Ollama Cloud — AI processing. Chat messages and symptom descriptions submitted for AI-assisted search may be sent via POST request bodies (outside search URLs) to Ollama to generate responses or extract search keywords. Avoid entering sensitive personal health details in URL-based keyword search bars (/herbs?q=). Ollama's own retention practices are governed by its privacy policy.
thirdParty.adsense: Google AdSense is not active. If advertising is enabled in future, Google and its partners may receive information about the public page being viewed and may use cookies or device identifiers to serve and measure ads. The intended placement is on public herb reference pages, not on health-input tools.
thirdParty.upstash: Upstash Redis — ephemeral rate-limiting counters (hashed request IP keys; US/cloud) to protect the site and AI endpoint against abuse.
thirdParty.sentry: Sentry — error monitoring and crash diagnostics with scrubbed request headers and cookies (US/cloud).
thirdParty.zoho: Zoho Mail (Canada) — transactional email delivery for safety-digest opt-in confirmation and privacy/editorial inquiries.
thirdParty.linkedinSso: LinkedIn OpenID Connect (optional, open edit contributors and clinical reviewers) — when any user, researcher, or clinician chooses to sign in on /clinical-review or via Suggest an edit on a herb page, LinkedIn supplies name and email address to validate identity and route edit suggestions.
thirdParty.crossBorder: Cross-border transfers: While our core PostgreSQL database runs in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, services such as Cloudflare, Ollama Cloud, LinkedIn SSO (when used by contributors or reviewers), Upstash, Sentry, and Stripe may process limited request metadata or submitted text outside Quebec and Canada under their respective data-protection frameworks.

cookiesSection.title: 5. Cookies
cookiesSection.localeCookie: herbally-locale — set only when you switch languages, to remember en or fr for up to 1 year.
cookiesSection.guestCookie: herbally-guest-id — an HttpOnly cookie that links your browser to an anonymous guest chat session so you can return to it.
cookiesSection.authCookies: Supabase authentication cookies — set only if you choose to sign in, so your session stays active.
cookiesSection.linkedinCookie: herbally-linkedin-reviewer — an HttpOnly signed session cookie (8-hour expiry) set only if a contributor or clinician signs in with LinkedIn SSO on /clinical-review or via Suggest an edit.
cookiesSection.adCookies: Advertising cookies — if ads are enabled, Google and its partners may set cookies or use identifiers to serve and measure ads. You can control these through your browser and Google's ad settings.
cookiesSection.noTracking: We do not use Facebook Pixel or invasive third-party trackers. Cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics provides aggregate page counts, and advertising cookies apply only if ads are enabled.

dataRetention.title: 6. Data Retention
dataRetention.text: Account and saved data may be retained until deleted. Anonymous guest chat sessions carry an explicit 30-day server retention schedule (retention_expires_at) from creation, and expiry of the guest cookie ends browser linkage earlier. For performance and safety consistency, single-turn stateless public educational Virtual Herbalist replies may be cached in a shared, prompt-hash-keyed server table (ai_response_cache) for up to 7 days without user, guest, or session identifiers, while personalized queries (with saved medications or herb context) and multi-turn conversations bypass shared caching completely. Deleting a conversation removes the chat session and messages immediately while unlinked public cache entries expire automatically after 7 days. Donation records may be retained for accounting. Ollama's retention practices are governed by its own policy.

yourRights.title: 7. Your Rights
yourRights.text: You can access, correct or delete the data you control in HerbAlly:
yourRights.access: Access: You can see your saved profile, garden, calculations and chat history in your account.
yourRights.deletion: You can remove garden entries and chat sessions (sessions and messages) using available app controls; unlinked 7-day prompt-hash AI cache entries cannot be matched to a conversation and expire automatically. Contact privacy@herbally.app to request deletion of your account or other saved information, including calculations. Clearing browser storage removes local data and browser caches held there.
yourRights.complaint: Complaint: Contact our Privacy Officer at privacy@herbally.app. You may also file a complaint with the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI) or the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC).
yourRights.portability: Portability & consent withdrawal: Under Quebec Law 25 and Canadian PIPEDA, you may request an export of personal information you provided in structured form, withdraw consent to non-essential storage, or unsubscribe from our digest with one click.

security.title: 8. Security
security.text: We implement appropriate technical measures to protect the service, including HTTPS encryption, Row-Level Security on our database, and regular dependency and security reviews.
security.breachNotice: Confidentiality incidents: In accordance with Quebec Law 25, we maintain technical safeguards and will notify affected individuals and regulators promptly if a confidentiality incident poses a risk of serious injury.

changes.title: 9. Changes to This Policy
changes.text: We may update this policy periodically. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date.

contact.title: 10. Contact
